title: Files and Streams
summary: Reading and writing files with File's one-line helpers and their async versions, paths with Path, directories, StreamReader and StreamWriter for large files line by line, encodings, the Stream abstraction, handling IOException, and reading CSV safely.

cards.q: What is the difference between File.ReadAllLines and File.ReadLines?
cards.a:
ReadAllLines loads every line into an array at once; ReadLines reads lazily as you loop

`ReadLines` returns a lazy sequence, so a huge file never has to fit in memory. The whole file as one string is `ReadAllText`.

cards.q: Why use Path.Combine instead of joining strings with a backslash?
cards.a:
The separator differs between operating systems, and Path.Combine uses the right one

Windows uses `\` and Linux and macOS use `/`. `Path.Combine` picks the right separator and avoids doubled slashes; it does not touch the disk.

cards.q: A StreamWriter is created without using and never disposed. What can happen?
cards.a:
The last lines stay in its buffer and never reach the file

Writers buffer data, and disposing flushes the buffer and closes the file. Without it the end of the data can be lost and the file can stay locked.
